_comment: Editable step content for the guided tour. Each step's 'id' must match a wiring entry in MainWindow._tutorial_step_wiring() (that map owns the target widget + tab-switch action; this file owns the user-facing copy). Reorder this array to change tour order; remove an entry to skip it; add a new id here + a matching wiring entry to add a step. Allowed preferred_side values: above, below, left, right, auto.

steps.title: Welcome to Open Strings
steps.description: This quick tour covers the core workflow of customizing strings and applying the result back to Star Citizen. Many of these steps run automatically, but can be done manually if needed. You can skip anytime.

steps.title: 1. Extract from Data.p4k
steps.description: Clicking Extract unpacks your installed game's stock localization file. On your very first extraction, Open Strings will download two small tools (~130 MB, one-time only). After that, extraction runs locally from your installed game data. The strings reload into the table automatically when extraction finishes.

steps.title: 2. Edit strings
steps.description: Each row is one localization record. Double-click a cell in the Custom Value column to edit — your changes are autosaved. Use the filter row above to narrow down your results. The ★ column marks ships as favorites so they sort to the top of the ASOP.

steps.title: 3. Preview pane
steps.description: Whenever you select a row, this pane on the right shows the rendered text of its current value.

steps.title: 4. Apply to Game
steps.description: Apply writes the merged result to the game's global.ini. A timestamped backup of the current global.ini is created first (up to 5 are kept, restorable from Restore Backup).

steps.title: 5. Enhancements
steps.description: Optional but recommended: the Enhancements tab toggles stat overlays for ships, components, weapons, and mission blueprints and rewards. Generate Enhancements runs the pipeline that produces those overlays from your extracted data.

steps.title: 6. Help & feedback
steps.description: The Help button opens a side-panel with the full guide, a Known Issues list, and a feedback link. That's everything you need to get started — good luck, citizen.
